## Objective
Generate diagram figures for ai review paper with synthetic data

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
library(splines)

# Simulate noisier data
set.seed(123)
n <- 20
x <- seq(0, 10, length.out = n)
y <- 2 * x + rnorm(n, sd = 6)  # MORE NOISE
data <- data.frame(Input = x, Output = y)

# Fit linear model
lm_fit <- lm(Output ~ Input, data = data)
data$linear_pred <- predict(lm_fit)

# Fit ridiculous overfit model using high-degree spline
overfit_fit <- lm(Output ~ bs(Input, df = n - 1), data = data)  # Overfit!
data$overfit_pred <- predict(overfit_fit)

# Plotting theme
theme_custom <- theme_minimal(base_family = "Arial") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
  )


p3 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Input, y = Output)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(aes(y = linear_pred, color = "Model"), size = 1) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = Input, yend = linear_pred, color = "Loss"), size = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = c("Model" = "orange", "Loss" = "grey")) +
  labs(x = "Input", y = "Output") +
  theme_custom +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(family = "Arial", size = 24)
  )

#ggsave("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/dissertation/exit_seminar/lin_reg.png", p3, width = 3.5, height = 2.25, units = "in", dpi = 300)

# Linear model plot
p1 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Input, y = Output)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(aes(y = linear_pred, color = "Model"), size = 1) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = Input, yend = linear_pred, color = "Loss"), size = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = c("Model" = "orange", "Loss" = "blue")) +
  labs( x = "Input", y = "Output") +
  theme_custom

# Overfit model plot
p2 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Input, y = Output)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(aes(y = overfit_pred, color = "Model"), size = 1) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = Input, yend = overfit_pred, color = "Loss"), size = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = c("Model" = "orange", "Loss" = "blue")) +
  labs(x = "Input", y = "Output") +
  theme_custom

print(p1)
print(p2)
# Save plot
ggsave("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab//fe_si_papers/artificial_intelligence_in_veterinary_diagnostic_histopathology_a_scoping_review_and_survey_of_current_implementation//figures//fig_2_regression/regression.png", arrangeGrob(p1, p2, ncol = 2), 
       width = 7, height = 3, dpi = 300)

p3 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Input, y = Output)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(aes(y = linear_pred, color = "Model"), size = 1) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = Input, yend = linear_pred, color = "Loss"), size = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = c("Model" = "orange", "Loss" = "blue")) +
  labs(x = "Input", y = "Output") +
  theme_custom +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(family = "Arial", size = 24)
  )

ggsave("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/dissertation/exit_seminar/lin_reg.png", p1, width = 3.5, height = 2.25, units = "in", dpi = 300)
```

```{r}


# Generate example data for a ReLU activation curve
x <- seq(-6, 6, length.out = 100)
y <- pmax(0, x)
data <- data.frame(x, y)

# Plot with minimal styling and axes but without ticks or labels
activation_plot <- ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_line(size = 1, color = "black") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    plot.background = element_blank()
  )

# Show the plot
activation_plot


# Save plot
ggsave("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/Projects/fe_si_papers/ai_in_vet_dx_histopath/figures//activation_function.png",  
       width = 1, height = 1, dpi = 300)
```
